evaluations.rationale: A is polished, clear, and register-appropriate. It preserves nearly all required claims, but the added qualifier often weakens the productivity claim slightly, and it does not explicitly frame the three items as what the post will explore.

evaluations.label: B

claims.evidence: What used to be an occasional perk is now part of the routine for millions of professionals.
A 2023 Gallup survey found that 52% of U.S. employees who can work remotely have hybrid arrangements
Remote workers tend to be more productive
employers can reduce office costs
Remote workers tend to be more productive and satisfied
remote employees save about 55 minutes a day
Teams can lose their sense of connection, and remote employees may feel isolated.
Managers need clear ways to keep distributed teams coordinated and engaged.
communication, trust, and reasonable boundaries
whether someone has worked remotely for years or is just getting started

evaluations.rationale: B is readable but materially softens and shifts several claims. It changes rare to occasional, moves productivity and satisfaction from company-level benefits to worker-level tendencies, weakens the commute-time figure with about, and omits motivated from the management claim.

limitations: Evaluation is based only on the supplied source text and pre-registered claim inventory. Some paraphrase judgments, especially around strength qualifiers such as often, report, and clear, require interpretation. No external verification of the Gallup statistic or commute-time claim was performed.
